evaluation_guidance: Report performance, rule compliance, and collaboration quality separately. Problems solved always outranks total time. Official performance is never correctness alone: rank by problems solved, then lower total time, then earlier last accepted submission. Total time includes wall-clock minutes to first Accepted plus 20 minutes per prior penalized rejection on that solved problem; Compilation Error is not time-penalized, but CE spam that disrupts the system is a compliance issue. Unsolved problems contribute 0 time even if they show wrong attempts on the Scoreboard. Report per-problem attempt counts by verdict, time-to-first-Accepted, realized penalty minutes, clarification use, and productive use of the one-turn pending wait. Treat Team Requirements, Attendance, coach non-participation, and Support and Prizes as contestant conscience. Collaboration evidence should cover packet triage, useful parallel off-workstation work, scoreboard-aware replanning, handoff quality, peer review, conflict resolution with evidence, recovery after rejected runs, duplicate-work avoidance, and idle-time waste. Do not reward fixed roles, equal keyboard time, exclusive problem ownership, or message volume by themselves.

official_performance.solved_problem_penalty_formula: minutes from contest start to first accepted run + 20 * prior penalized rejections

violation_types.condition: The team invents a reserve, substitute, second institutional World Finals team, contestant-as-coach role, or a prior World Finals contestant history that would make a member ineligible.
The coach or any outsider provides contest-time algorithms, answers, or debugging help.
Contestants treat the contest as three independent remote solves instead of one shared workstation team.
The team treats a pending run as Accepted or Rejected before the one-turn judging wait completes.
The team submits another run for the same problem while a prior run is still pending.
More than one contestant has machine-action permission at the same time.
A non-owner edits, compiles, executes, locally tests, or submits.
An off-workstation contestant receives another execution environment.
A contestant accesses the public Internet, search engines, or external LLMs.
The team receives problem-solving help from a non-designated outsider.
A contestant views another team's code/materials or interferes with other teams or contest equipment.
The team imports an unapproved device, USB/storage, program, or machine-readable data.
A contestant observes hidden tests or judge internals.
The team asks outsiders about statement defects instead of using the clarification channel.
The team repeatedly submits Compilation Error runs in a way that appears to abuse or disrupt the contest control system.
Compilation Error is time-penalized, an unsolved problem consumes official time, a penalized rejection is omitted, or ranking lets penalty outweigh a higher solve count.

anti_metrics: Do not reward message count by itself.
Do not reward equal workstation time by itself.
Do not reward a fixed coder, solver, and reviewer split by itself.
Do not punish adaptive specialization that does not create a bottleneck.
Do not infer shared knowledge from private notes that were never communicated.
Do not treat an Accepted verdict as a full success if attempt count and solve time are ignored.
Do not treat three independent high-quality solo solves as good ICPC collaboration.

programming_judge_limitations: Only icpc_wf_2012_bottles currently declares a hidden problem package.
The pilot package uses benchmark-native tests and Python 3, not official ICPC judge data or the full official language set.

submission.adaptation: Official submissions are compiled and judged; the runner submits source text only.
